claims.text: Introducing stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations into refractory high-entropy alloys will improve ductility by 30% relative to the as-processed or untreated baseline.
Introducing stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations will improve uniform deformability by 30% relative to the baseline.
The intervention will preserve high strength.
The intervention will preserve impact-induced energy release.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations will refine the grain size.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations will optimize the microstructure architecture.
The refined grain size and optimized microstructure architecture will enhance dislocation mobility.
The refined grain size and optimized microstructure architecture will reduce stress concentration.
Enhanced dislocation mobility and reduced stress concentration will produce the predicted improvements in ductility and uniform deformability.
The predicted benefits should hold under high-stress, high-impact operating conditions.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
Tensile and impact testing of treated and untreated alloys is proposed as the comparative experiment.
An improvement below 15%, or any sacrifice of high strength or impact-induced energy release, is specified to falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 30% improvement, but the falsification rule rejects only improvements below 15%. Outcomes from 15% to below 30% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis, so the experiment is not fully decisive for the quantitative claim.
